claim.quote: We currently hold the world record for the highest instantaneous luminosity ever achieved at a particle accelerator: 5.319 x 1034 cm−2s−1 achieved on June 30, 2026.

date.note: Date of the record as stated by the Belle II collaboration on its own home page, read 2026-09-16.
date.quote: We currently hold the world record for the highest instantaneous luminosity ever achieved at a particle accelerator: 5.319 x 1034 cm−2s−1 achieved on June 30, 2026.

name: SuperKEKB world-record instantaneous luminosity
notes: Earlier milestones on the same machine, not recorded as separate results: 2.22 × 10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹ on 15 June 2020 (KEK IPNS press release, the first time SuperKEKB passed KEKB's 2.11 × 10³⁴) and 5.1 × 10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹ quoted in the March 2025 Belle II European Strategy input.
Attributed to experiment:belle-ii because the atlas has no result owner for a bare accelerator; the machine is accelerator:superkekb.

significance.note: Not applicable to a technology milestone.

summary.plain: On 30 June 2026 the SuperKEKB collider in Japan packed more collisions into each second than any accelerator has ever managed, beating its own earlier records.
summary.technical: SuperKEKB reached a peak instantaneous luminosity of 5.319 × 10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹, the highest achieved by any colliding-beam accelerator, using the nano-beam scheme with a large crossing angle.

title: World record for the highest instantaneous luminosity ever achieved at a particle accelerator
why_it_matters: Instantaneous luminosity sets the rate at which Belle II accumulates its data set; the record is the operational proof of the nano-beam scheme on which the 50 ab⁻¹ programme depends.
